As a visitor or signed-in user, I can navigate app routes and be redirected to sign-in when a protected route needs a session.

React Router maps all declared routes directly; protected pages call useRequireSession, which redirects unauthenticated visitors to /sign-in with a callbackURL preserving the original path. The catch-all route renders a dedicated not-found recovery page instead of reusing sign-in.
Catch-all routed unknown paths to SignIn, making mistyped or stale URLs look like authentication entry points.
Added a dedicated NotFound page, wired the catch-all route to it, and covered the route with a focused regression test.

Unknown frontend routes now render a clear not-found recovery screen with public entry links. Source audit plus pnpm lint, pnpm test, and pnpm build passed after the UX/logistical fixes. Broader browser/E2E gaps remain tracked on the Coverage Gaps sheet.
As a keyboard user, I can reveal and hide password text without leaving the keyboard.

No current error found; the shared reveal toggle is keyboard-focusable and announces pressed state.

Initial code review found the reveal button has tabIndex={-1}; this is a concrete UX issue to fix after baseline verification. Source audit plus pnpm lint, pnpm test, and pnpm build passed after the UX/logistical fixes. Broader browser/E2E gaps remain tracked on the Coverage Gaps sheet.
